audit_decision: Inspected native DynamicArray and nested BasicIterator/Iterator declarations against current source. Cursor construction, mutable-to-const conversion, captured-end arithmetic, access/arrow and assignment already have callable adapters; pointer cache and ABI domains remain partial.

Selected actual missing internal-source nonassignable SetValue: external EmplaceValue reconstruction callbacks cannot safely capture an internal donor through the same mutably borrowed array. No cosmetic aliases were added.
behavior: Two unsafe indexed SetValue reconstruction methods support borrowed or mutable internal donors. They share the existing allocation/gap/construction engine with assignable SetValue, selecting only existing-target replacement policy separately.

The internal donor constructor finishes before borrowing and destroying the old target, including self-source. No donor reference remains during destruction. Raw replacement helpers reconstruct through the explicit transfer callback and destroy the temporary afterward.

Native deleted-assignment types establish all three move_if_noexcept choices: potentially throwing move with available copy selects copy; unavailable copy selects move; noexcept move with available copy selects move. Borrowed copy then noexcept move transfer is tested separately.

102 native rows cover80 successful combinations of four source/transfer domains, four existing targets and one new gap target, with each of four internal donors.22 rows cover initial-constructor and permitted transfer throws, default failures and negative targets.

Every potentially destructive Rust call begins inside ManuallyDrop before catch_unwind. On transfer failure observations skip the dead slot, preserve metadata and other values, and use raw block pointers for identity. The target is explicitly rebuilt before automatic ownership resumes. All fixtures return their live-item count to zero.

Existing-target constructor failure leaves old storage live, retaining mutable donor changes. Transfer failure destroys the old target and temporary while Size remains unchanged. New targets default-construct gaps and construct the source value directly without invoking transfer.

Normal18-target DynamicArray suite and strict Miri include the previously integrated assignable internal-source adapters. All52 original legacy declarations join to normal/Miri results; nine new Rust cases cover102 native rows and checked invalid source rejection.
limitations: The caller explicitly selects reconstruction and transfer operations. Automatic C++ traits and noexcept ABI are not inferred from Rust Default/Clone; throwing from a native noexcept move constructor is outside the probe domain.
Destructors must not unwind. A transfer panic requires dead-slot repair before access or cleanup; the public safety contract explicitly covers automatic Drop during unwinding before a catch.

Only initialized logical donors are supported. Invalid native indices/references, direct construction of noncopyable/nonmovable items from SetValue arguments, address-dependent constructors and payload/descriptor ABI are not claimed.

Existing iterator cached-pointer behavior after destructive owner mutation remains outside current checked cursor lifetime contracts. Existing safe EraseLast convenience remains partial for callback-time Size, covered separately by its explicit destruction adapter.
validation_scope: Final production methods share the native gap factory and existing raw replacement primitive. Normal tests, scoped Clippy/fmt, strict-provenance Miri and compiler body captures are archived with source hashes; original native52 pass. No shared parity or raw lifetime helper changes.
